Thanks team — quick commercial view from AE:

Option 1 (preferred for speed): Redwood invoices the end customer; CloudSupply receives a settlement payment from Redwood. Order Form contains: "Customer is the payer for Redwood services. CloudSupply will be paid a settlement amount agreed between the parties; CloudSupply is responsible for invoicing its customers for any platform/marketplace fee it charges." This keeps Redwood's revenue recognition clean.

Option 2 (preferred for partner experience): CloudSupply invoices customer and remits net to Redwood. Order Form: "CloudSupply is the reseller and will be listed as the billing party. CloudSupply will remit payment to Redwood in accordance with the settlement schedule." This is better for CloudSupply but requires payment security and WHT/tax handling language.

Option 3 (for risk-averse legal): Reseller-principal with tax backstop. CloudSupply invoices and is primary obligor; CloudSupply indemnifies Redwood for taxes/collection issues and provides a limited audit right.

Happy to lead a short call with Anita and legal to decide. For renewals/expansions let's prefer Option 1 unless counsel insists on reseller model.

Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Folks —

High-level legal direction (summary of redlines attached):

1) Pass-through acknowledgement: Acceptable if CloudSupply's addendum includes explicit naming of Redwood services and a statement that CloudSupply is the billing intermediary. We will ask that the Order Form include the phrase: "Redwood shall invoice the Customer unless the Order Form expressly states CloudSupply is the billing party."

2) Tax allocation: We will accept a reseller invoicing model only if CloudSupply: (a) assumes responsibility for local sales/VAT and (b) provides a quarterly tax reconciliation and backstop for amounts Redwood cannot collect directly.

3) Audit & records: Limited audit rights (one annual review, 30-day notice) tied to billing reconciliation only.

4) Liability: No broad carveout. Any pass-through must not expand Redwood's indemnity exposure beyond what is in the MSA. Suggest a short clause: "Neither party's liability to the other shall be increased by reason of the distribution channel."

Next steps I propose:
- I will produce a redline to CloudSupply's addendum accepting an intermediation clause with the three guardrails above.
- Aditya to confirm commercial preference and settlement cadence (30/60/90).
- Olga to schedule call with Anita + CloudSupply counsel for Thursday.

I attached redlines_olga_20261013.docx with inline comments and a suggested Order Form snippet.

Rishi
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
